text:
frank: FYI I opened a migration-runbook PR that walks customers from Hosted -> Private (VPC). It includes a minimal SDK snippet for switching endpoints, networking preflight checks, and an HSM/KMS checklist. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5127

leah: skimmed the SDK snippet. tiny request: show both Go and Python examples and highlight the auth token change (hosted token vs private service account). maybe add a note about different rate limits for private clusters.

frank: added Go + Python examples and a short note: "Private deployments use service-account tokens minted by the control plane; hosted API tokens will stop working after migration unless swapped." Example Python: `client = Redwood(api_base='https://private.example.local', token='/var/run/redwood/token')`

toni: networking note: strongly call out hairpin NAT and internal registry DNS. customer will often mirror images to an internal registry; add example /etc/hosts line and a kube imagePullSecret snippet.

frank: added hosts example `10.10.10.10 registry.internal.local registry.redwood.ai` and a base64 imagePullSecret snippet. also added an nftables example for minimal firewalling.

infra-bot: Lint: OK. Broken links: 1 (will create issue if not fixed). CI: pending.

leah: HSM ports: recommend documenting 5698/tcp as required, 5699/tcp as optional admin. also warn that some appliances enforce strict client cert validation; add a note to check HSM TLS cert CN and truststore.

frank: added HSM cert guidance and a short `openssl s_client -connect hsm.local:5698 -servername hsm.local` command to verify chain. also called out time sync: many HSMs reject sessions with >5s drift.

toni: airgap tip: offline bundle filenames from S3 can be long. explicitly recommend placing bundle under `/opt/offline-bundles/redwood-<date>.tar.gz` and mention 256 char limit on some filesystems. add SELinux `restorecon -R` note for RHEL.

frank: done. I also added a tiny conn-checker script that verifies TCP, TLS, and the local health endpoint:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
nc -zv registry.internal.local 443
openssl s_client -connect registry.internal.local:443 -servername registry.internal.local < /dev/null | grep "Verify return code: 0"
curl -sSf http://localhost:8080/health
echo SMOKE OK
```

leah: perfect. one security wording nit: avoid "allow all egress" phrasing; recommend explicit allowlist like `rdw-inference-updates.redwood.ai:443` and `registry.internal.local:443`.

frank: updated wording. I'll merge after CI green. filing follow-up issue #5128 to add annotated screenshots of the conn-checker output and a downloadable example Runbook PDF.

docs-bot: CI: queued. Will post results and link-fix suggestions.
